title: FiniteEncoding coordinates for smooth purity
statement: Use [def-pur-transport-concrete-coefficients]. For any finite discrete commutative ring $A$, the map from the constant sheaf to continuous $A$-valued functions is constant functions followed by the sheafification ring comparison. It is a monoid isomorphism. Internal modules at the point are encoded as ordinary modules by their actual scalar action, with the same underlying additive groups and maps; this is an equivalence and its additive forget functor is literally the original one. Apply the existing sectionwise finite coefficient equivalence using these two fixed encodings, and derive it termwise. The direct-image comparison is the identity on sections and scalar actions; the inverse-image comparison is its adjunction mate.

source.place: Coefficient, functor, counit and normalization clauses; coordinate interface TransportFiniteEncoding

proof.text: For finiteConstants_spec, use the proved local injectivity and local surjectivity instances of the literal additive constant-function map in FiniteDiscreteCondensedRing. GrothendieckTopology.W_of_isLocallyBijective and W_iff show that sheafification inverts this map. Compose with the sheafification counit isomorphism. Both factors are monoid morphisms, so their composite is invertible and multiplicative. This keeps the specified map, rather than choosing an unspecified comparison isomorphism.

The fixed finiteModuleEncoding is the concrete internalToModule functor of InternalModuleAbEquivalence. Its existing fully faithful and essentially surjective instances give IsEquivalence. Its underlying additive group functor is the internal-module forgetful functor by reflexivity.

Keep the existing definitions of finitePointIso, finiteEncoding, finiteEncodingDerived and the pushforward and pullback comparisons, now using the proved properties of their fixed input maps and functor.
